item.title: A million tiny crystals reveal how semiconductors form distinct cores and shells
item.description: Perovskites and related materials called perovskitoids are promising semiconductor materials for solar cells, LEDs and light detectors. Their ingredients and internal crystal structures determine how they absorb and emit light. A chip just 2 centimeters across can hold roughly a million tiny crystals—becoming a miniature material library that can show how some mixtures separate into distinct cores and shells, changing the light they absorb. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Global analysis reveals how lakes amplify glacier ice loss
item.description: Glacial lakes can accelerate the retreat of glaciers. item.title: Mapping the microbes' arms race with viruses at planetary scale
item.description: Microbiomes are complex ecosystems, in which bacteria and archaea are constantly interacting with, and infected by, viruses. These viruses can significantly impact microbiome processes, not only by killing their host but also sometimes by temporarily providing additional capabilities to their host. As many viruses have not been grown in a lab, connecting them to their natural hosts has been difficult. A new bioinformatics toolkit and database are now available to help researchers make those associations at an unprecedented scale. Fuente: Phys.org.
